tagline: Find any host — and every asset behind a dashboard number.
problem: "Which assets is that number?" is the first question after any dashboard — and answering it usually means a hand-written query or an export. Without the list, a metric can't be acted on.
does: Explorer › Assets searches every asset by hostname, IP, OS or network. It is also where Ensemble Report's At a glance cards land: each card opens the exact assets behind its number — computed by the specialist that owns it — riskiest (highest ACR) first, ready to page, search and export.

glance.caption: Explorer › Assets opened from an Ensemble Report card: the evidence card names the number and the specialist that owns it, and the asset list below pages and searches on the server and exports to CSV.

capabilities: hostname, IP, OS or network in one box.
KEV-exploitable assets, assets scored 60 or more, crown jewels (all, with KEV, or scanned without credentials), assets flagged by four or more specialists, EOL software, quantum-vulnerable crypto.
each list is computed with the owning specialist's own rule — Laelaps, Exposure Score, Charon or Heimdall.
the list is stored on the server, so 50 or 150,000 assets page, search and export the same way.
every host opens Asset Dossier, where its findings can be remediated with Remote Remediation or tagged; a Tenable link opens it in Tenable.
how: Explorer › Assets reads your local navi.db and changes nothing. Evidence lists are built on request by the specialist that owns the number, so they reflect navi.db now — a card built at the last Run the Ensemble run can differ slightly.
who: Analysts and VM leads who need to see — and act on — the assets behind a metric.
better: Ensemble Report's cards open here; Asset Dossier takes over for one asset; Notify & Report can email the list.
cta: Give Explorer › Assets a number — it brings back every asset behind it.
